name: Rosewood Sand Hill
positioning: Rosewood Sand Hill: a hotel on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, in the foothills of the Santa Cruz Mountains and one mile from Stanford University, with a wood-fired restaurant, a spa and residential villas
best_for: Travelers visiting Stanford University or the venture-capital corridor
Cyclists who want a road bike and local guidance
Longer stays in a villa with a full kitchen and laundry room

facts.text: The hotel sits in the foothills of the Santa Cruz Mountains.
The hotel is one mile from Stanford University.
The hotel is on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, in the heart of the venture-capital corridor.
The interiors are Northern California-inspired, combining neutral hues with tones of walnut, cherry and cedar.
Rooms overlook the mountains or courtyard gardens and have private balconies, artwork and marble bathrooms.
Suites have a separate parlor and a furnished balcony or patio.
Signature Suites have a fireplace and a marble bath.
Madera has an open wood-burning kitchen and serves American cuisine indoors or out.
Madera serves seasonal dishes with ingredients sourced from local farms and suppliers.
The Pool Bar & Grill serves snacks and cocktails poolside.
Bici Coffee is a coffee stop for cyclists, locals and the Sand Hill community.
Asaya Spa offers holistic treatments and has fragrant gardens that mimic the surroundings.

highlights.text: The Colnago Experience gives guests access to a C72 road bike handcrafted in Italy, paired with local guidance.
The residential villas have a full chef's kitchen, a laundry room and a fully fenced private backyard, suited to long-term stays.
Madera Bar serves handcrafted cocktails and light bites on its terrace, with views of the Santa Cruz mountains.
The hotel offers a wine tasting experience at Ridge Vineyards.
Private dining rooms within Madera host gatherings of up to 16 guests, and private terraces look out to the Santa Cruz mountains.

considerations.text: The hotel is in the middle of a business park rather than in a town center.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes a business-focused atmosphere that may suit leisure travelers less.
